> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3175d59d036d3c2819d5e7913c8c406c1ea634d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `756db9fb7dea7d41b73d6cb9a1db96c8f67bbf3a` — the merge of head `c34c2e14a8447260e8ab5fb959fd3104776e8c0b` into base `d3175d59d036d3c2819d5e7913c8c406c1ea634d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 756db9fb7dea7d41b73d6cb9a1db96c8f67bbf3a && git checkout 756db9fb7dea7d41b73d6cb9a1db96c8f67bbf3a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d3175d59d036d3c2819d5e7913c8c406c1ea634d c34c2e14a8447260e8ab5fb959fd3104776e8c0b && git checkout -B drift-repro d3175d59d036d3c2819d5e7913c8c406c1ea634d && git merge --no-ff c34c2e14a8447260e8ab5fb959fd3104776e8c0b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3175d59d036d3c2819d5e7913c8c406c1ea634d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d3175d59d036d3c2819d5e7913c8c406c1ea634d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c34c2e14a8447260e8ab5fb959fd3104776e8c0b`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #29568 (body, triage 6585925375, claims 6586570416 / 6586610006, dev report 6587487066), the PR body, its 6-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head. The cited code was read on `origin/main` (`d3175d59`); nothing was built or run.

CI: all 50 check-runs on the head have completed: 38 success, 12 skipped (opt-in or not-triggered legs), 0 red. That includes Test Core 1–8/8, Type Check workspace and consumer gates, Test UI, Lint ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Dogfood Regression Gate.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set: unchanged. Right.** The diff swaps the `CUSTOMISE_BESIDE_REMEDY` constant for `customizeInPairRemedy(id)` at the same two concatenation sites (`requireWritablePackage`, `requireDuplicableSource`). Status 422, `code` (`WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` / `DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NOT_A_BASE`), `details` (`packageId`, `docs`), the predicate (`isWritablePackage`) and the call order at all 8 doors are untouched in the hunks. No new code, no `packages/spec/**`, no `metadata-protocol` edit. `Clause-②: no` holds.
2. **Public surface: the message text of 8 refusals, and nothing parses it. Right.** `git grep` on main finds no reader of this text in `packages/rest`, `packages/client`, `packages/qa`, `apps` or `ui`. Clients branch on `code`. The one text reader is ui `splitRefusal` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/refusalLead.ts`). It leads with the first `.`/`!`/`?` before whitespace, after stripping `[writable_package_required]`. That sentence ("Cannot … : it is read-only (provided by code or an installed app).") is byte-identical on head. The new sentence's `;` is not followed by `[`, so the joined-issues split cannot fire either. The pair id's dots (`com.x.custom'`) are never followed by whitespace, so they do not end a sentence. The lead and `full` behave as before.
3. **The sentence is true for every base kind measured. Right.** I checked each Step 0 row against the clause that covers it:
   - code app (`com.example.showcase`) and installed managed (`com.acme.installed`): ensure 201, declared save 200, served. The main clause covers both.
   - system `com.objectstack.setup`: ensure 201, `app/setup` 403 `ITEM_LOCKED`. Covered by "a locked item, is refused naming … the lock".
   - `action` 403 `declared_type_not_yet_available` and `permission` 403 `declared_type_not_overridable`: main's `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` messages end "rename the item" / "create your own … ("new similar")". So "refused naming its route" holds.
   - second `sys` namespace 422 `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` and no namespace 409: covered by "a package that cannot have a pair is refused at that door, naming why".
   - id the pairing rule refuses (`customizationPackageId` not ok): the sentence names the ensure door only and no pair id. Pinned in the new test.

   It never promises a route that refuses the caller. All 8 doors run `requireManageMetadata` then `refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite` before the read-only gate (main `packages.ts`, every site). The ensure door runs the same two gates. So anyone who receives the 422 is admitted at the ensure door on caller grounds.
4. **The save-contract spelling matches main. Right.** `closedOverlayWriteClauses` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`) spells the pair `'PAIR' (?package=PAIR)` and the declaration ``overrides: { package: 'BASE', basedOn }``. The new sentence uses the same tokens. ADR-0146 D2 puts the declaration in the item body with `package` = the base id and `basedOn` = the base's `manifest.version`. D3 makes the ensure door the pair's one creation path. D11 closes the package-less write `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. The integration test reads the three tokens out of a live 422 and follows them (ensure 201, PUT `?package=PAIR` with `overrides` 200, served label changed). It also has the package-less control (403 naming the pair).
5. **Length: no cap applies, and none truncates. Right.** `deps.error` → `HttpDispatcher#error` → `apiErrorResponse` (`packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.ts`) does no slicing. `CLIENT_MESSAGE_MAX` (500, `@objectstack/types` `truncateClientMessage`) is reached only through `mapDataError` / `resolveErrorResponse`, not through these dispatcher doors. `packages/rest`'s direct mount for packages is `POST /packages/publish` alone. The dev's base measurement shows the duplicate door already answering 815 characters whole on main. The fix-first ordering that the save door's doc block asks for is about that 500 bound, so it does not bind on these doors. The new sentence is one fix clause followed by one limits clause, in the house shape.
6. **Docs (`install-modes.mdx`): accurate against ADR-0146 D2/D3/D6/D9/D11. Right.** The link target heading exists on main (`metadata-lifecycle.mdx` "Customizing an installed package: the paired `.custom` override (ADR-0146)"), and `Check Documentation Links` is green.
7. **Overlap with main: none. Right.** The merge-base is `dbca3ef0` and `origin/main` is 9 commits ahead. None of those commits touches the 6 PR paths. The two adjacent ones are #29535 (migration entry 18's prose, `packages/spec`) and #28979 (`defaultRecordPageSaveRefusal` in `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts`). Neither changes `closedOverlayWriteClauses`, `customizationPackageId` or the ensure door. The PR does not need a merge.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29568-readonly-remedy-pair-route.md`: `'@objectstack/runtime': patch`, with `Clause-②: no (message text only)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on line-initial lines, the same in the PR body. Right. The diff changes the message text of a released package and nothing an author can write. The other files are tests and `content/docs`, which publish nothing. `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0], the ui `RefusalMessage.test.tsx` fixture: answer B, and A as written is not available.** #29489 closed as completed via #29537 before this card was triaged, so it cannot carry the refresh. Leave the fixture as it is for this PR. It pins `splitRefusal`'s lead only, the lead is byte-identical on head, and `Test UI` is green. It was never a verbatim copy: it cuts the old sentence at "save an item under its own name." while the server's text went on. A refresh is optional ui-lane hygiene for the seat to carry. It does not block this PR and is not filed.
- **Deviation: not merged with main (9 behind).** Verified, with no overlap (① 7). Accepted.
- **Deviation: harness defaults not followed (no assignee, reviewer or subscription).** This follows the standard order. Accepted.
- **Deviation: the integration file's 17 s duration.** The cost is import (`createStandaloneStack`), the tests take 1.24 s, and the workspace deps are pre-imported at module load as `check-test-source-alias` requires. The file declares no budget. Accepted.
- **Gate note: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exited 3 before the fixture fetch.** That is a clone prerequisite, not a red, and CI's lint legs on the head carry the verdict. Accepted.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0]:** the same fixture as above, with the same answer.

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix:**
- The PR body's Acceptance notes and the open question name #29489 as a carrier, but #29489 is closed. Reword it to name the seat (a PR-body edit, non-blocking).

**Nit (optional):** in "— delete a package you own, or customize what it ships in its paired package …", "it" can be read as the caller's own package. The pair id and the ensure route make the meaning clear, so this is a nit only (the old text said "this package").
